PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]

Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Carrier testing for FRAXA premutation allele associated with premature ovarian failure.

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes. PCR amplification of the FMR1 gene CGG repeat region was performed using fluorescently labeled primers flanking the repeat. Fragment analysis was conducted by capillary electrophoresis. Southern blot analysis was performed using EcoRI and EagI digestion followed by hybridization with probe StB12.3 to detect expanded alleles beyond the range of PCR amplification.

RESULTS
FMR1 Gene Analysis (FRAXA)
Test performed: PCR and Southern blot analysis
Result: Single normal-sized FRAXA allele detected

Allele size: 29 CGG repeats
Interpretation: Normal

Southern blot analysis confirmed the presence of a single FMR1 locus, consistent with a 46,XY karyotype. No additional alleles were detected.

TECHNICAL NOTES
FRAXA Allele Size Reference Ranges:
- Normal: 5-44 CGG repeats
- Intermediate/Gray zone: 45-54 CGG repeats
- Premutation: 55-200 CGG repeats
- Full mutation: >200 CGG repeats

SUMMARY
Molecular analysis of the FMR1 gene revealed a single normal-sized allele with 29 CGG repeats. The presence of only one FMR1 allele is consistent with a 46,XY karyotype as confirmed by cytogenetic analysis. This finding indicates that the patient has a male chromosomal complement and therefore cannot be a carrier of an FMR1 premutation associated with premature ovarian failure, which affects individuals with two X chromosomes.

The single FRAXA allele finding is consistent with the 46,XY karyotype from cytogenetics.
